subject: MSA + Order Form: governing law, injunctive relief & evidence preservation

Subject: MSA + Order Form: governing law & urgent preservation request

Jonas —

Thanks for the redline call earlier. Attached are our tracked changes to the MSA and Order Form (CloudOptic_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx). A couple of items to flag up front:

1) Governing law: CloudOptic is pushing for Delaware law. We understand Redwood often prefers CA or NY — can you confirm your position and any flexibility?
2) Emergency injunctive relief: counsel wants an explicit carveout to ensure CloudOptic can seek provisional remedies in court for IP/data preservation.
3) Evidence preservation: procurement has asked us to confirm retention and audit-log access — specifically a 180-day raw-audit retention plus an obligation to preserve KMS and access logs on notice.

Can you route this to the right legal ops folks and confirm whether you can accept the preservation checklist we included? If Redwood can accept the preservation language and an injunctive-relief carveout (with an agreed escalation ladder), we can move quickly to signature.

Attachments: CloudOptic_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx; Evidence_Preservation_Checklist.pdf

Best,
Sofia

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: governing law & urgent preservation request

Sofia —

Thanks for the redlines and the preservation checklist. Looping in Laura and David from Legal and Marcus from Product/Infra to confirm feasibility. High-level response for CloudOptic procurement:

- Governing law: Redwood prefers California law for operational contracts; we are open to Delaware for enterprise customers if coupled with our standard arbitration clause.
- Injunctive relief carveout: we can accept a narrowly tailored carveout permitting either party to seek provisional injunctive relief in court (to protect IP or prevent data exfiltration), provided the carveout: (i) is limited to provisional measures, (ii) requires prompt notice to the other party and (iii) includes our escalation ladder to attempt expedited internal remedies first.
- Evidence preservation: we can commit to a 180-day accessible audit-log retention and will preserve KMS and request logs for 90 days on written notice; longer hold can be agreed on a case-by-case basis (we propose an escrow/forensics path if CloudOptic needs >90 days).

Laura / David — are you comfortable with the draft injunctive carveout below? If yes, I'll circulate a proposed redline (short text) to Sofia for regressive review.

Proposed injunctive carveout (conceptual):
1) Either party may seek provisional equitable relief (injunction) in a court of competent jurisdiction to prevent imminent and irreparable harm to intellectual property or to prevent unauthorized exfiltration of customer data.
2) Such relief shall be limited to provisional measures pending arbitration or final determination.
3) Prior to filing, the requesting party shall: (a) provide written notice to the other party describing the emergency; (b) attempt to resolve the matter via the escalation ladder (Tier 1: account CSM/Engineering on-call; Tier 2: Legal ops; Tier 3: VP-level escalation) for a period of up to 24 hours where operational remedies could avert immediate harm.

If you don't hear otherwise today I'll draft a clean redline and attach the proposed evidence-preservation text for CloudOptic to review.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Contracts | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0199

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-10T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: internal: RE: MSA + Order Form — preservation + forum language

Jonas / David —

Quick internal note from Legal: I think this is negotiable with two guardrails: (A) keep the carveout narrow and expressly temporary ("provisional/preliminary only"), and (B) avoid language that waives the arbitration clause broadly. Suggested concrete edits:

- Insert wording: "Notwithstanding the arbitration provision, either party may seek provisional equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction, solely to preserve the status quo or prevent imminent harm, and any such court action shall be limited to such provisional relief and shall not decide the merits of the dispute."
- For governing law, consent to Delaware is acceptable if the venue for provisional relief is limited to a local convenient forum (e.g., Northern District of California or Delaware) — propose: governing law = Delaware; venue for provisional relief = Northern District of California or Delaware (mutual).
- Preservation obligations: Redwood will commit to preserving audit logs and KMS records for 180 days, but we add a reasonable-cost provision for extraordinary preservation and offer a forensic escrow with predefined rates.

If you approve, I'll draft precise redline language for both the MSA and an accompanying addendum: "Evidence Preservation & Emergency Escalation Addendum". We should also add an SLA trigger for forensic assistance (response within 4 hours for confirmed exfiltration events).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
